content.title: Hand-Bounded Medium Window | Local Conversion, Geometry Proof, Return
content.summary: Form a visible two-hand boundary before changing medium, keep conversion strictly inside the registered moving window, prove the rule with multiple geometries, then dismiss it and return to baseline.

quick_start.input_format: Clearly adult original controller + stable environment anchors + visible two-hand boundary + alternate medium + at least three geometries or coverage regions + late large-coverage apex + return confirmation
quick_start.recommended_input: In a locked greenhouse shot, a clearly adult researcher stretches an amber window between both hands. Only its interior becomes cyan botanical cross-section linework; horizontal, vertical, and diagonal shapes prove the rule before a late face-and-leaf apex collapses into one filament and a real white flower opens one petal.
required_anchors: Before activation, establish one clearly adult original controller, a stable environment, and visibly inactive hands.
The two-hand geometry must form before the medium changes, and every active edge must stay bound to fingertips or hand edges.
Keep the alternate medium strictly inside the moving boundary, preserve exact registration across the edge, and leave the exterior in its baseline state.
Prove one rule with at least three geometries or coverage regions; reserve the largest coverage for late in the sequence, then dismiss it and confirm the original medium with one reaction or residue.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, boundary material, and alternate medium with an original concept.
Establish the baseline first, then let the two-hand geometry cause strictly local conversion.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 template and fill only the declared variable slots.
Before generation, check edge registration, geometry differences, apex timing, complete return, sound, and anti-copy distance.
applicable_scope: Form a visible two-hand boundary before changing medium, keep conversion strictly inside the registered moving window, prove the rule with multiple geometries, then dismiss it and return to baseline.
Original 4–15 second mechanism films that can establish a baseline, prove at least three local states, and return completely.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that use stable registration to prove a local medium switch.
not_suitable_for: Requests to copy a source identity, styling, exact gestures, boundary appearance, or illustration design.
Concepts that cannot preserve cross-edge registration or that require a full-frame style takeover.
Loose effect showcases without visible two-hand control, geometry proof, or a return to baseline.

creative_dna.mechanism: A stable live-action baseline becomes an interactive proof surface: two visible hands first define a bounded aperture, only the registered area inside that moving geometry switches medium, repeated size and orientation changes prove the rule, a late large-coverage state supplies the apex, and a controlled dismissal restores the baseline for one confirming reaction or residue.

invariants.rule: Establish one clearly adult original subject, one stable environment and visibly empty or inactive hands before the boundary activates.
invariants.ablation_failure: If the baseline is missing, viewers cannot distinguish the transformation from an already-stylized full-frame filter.

invariants.rule: Make the two-hand geometry visibly form before the medium switch, and keep the luminous or material boundary attached to the controlling fingertips or hand edges.
invariants.ablation_failure: If the region appears independently of the hands, the central cause-and-control relationship collapses.

invariants.rule: Confine the alternate medium strictly inside the moving boundary while preserving continuous registration across the edge and leaving the exterior in its baseline state.
invariants.ablation_failure: If conversion leaks outside or registration slides, the aperture stops reading as a controllable local window.

invariants.rule: Use at least three materially different aperture geometries or orientations, with each state revealing a new region while obeying the same clipping rule.
invariants.ablation_failure: One static rectangle is only a filter demo; repeated rule-consistent geometry is what proves reusable control.

invariants.rule: Reserve the largest or most identity-sensitive coverage for a late apex, then visibly contract or dismiss the boundary instead of allowing an uncontrolled full-scene takeover.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without a late apex and controlled release, the sequence lacks escalation and the ending state becomes ambiguous.

invariants.rule: End in the original medium and spatial registration with one short subject reaction or physical residue that confirms the effect has ended.
invariants.ablation_failure: If the film ends inside the alternate medium, control and reversibility are not proven.

slots.name: adult_subject
slots.description: One clearly adult original controller with three stable appearance anchors and readable hands.

slots.name: base_environment
slots.description: A stable, simply registered space whose lines and lighting make local conversion easy to verify.

slots.name: boundary_material
slots.description: A luminous, drawn, mechanical or material edge visibly attached to both hands.

slots.name: alternate_medium
slots.description: A medium with clearly different rendering physics, such as scientific linework, paper blueprint, stained glass or clay relief.

slots.name: proof_regions
slots.description: At least three differently shaped or oriented local regions that all obey the same clipping and registration rule.

slots.name: apex_region
slots.description: The largest late-stage coverage, ideally crossing an identity-sensitive or information-rich area.

slots.name: ending_confirmation
slots.description: One restrained reaction or physical residue after the boundary is dismissed.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.description: Original edge-drawing, stretch, lock, medium-shift and release cues; semantic source audio is not reused.

anti_copy_exclusions: Do not reproduce any source-specific performer identity, appearance, wardrobe or proportions.
Do not reuse the source environment, boundary styling, alternate-medium character design or exact transformation surface.
Do not copy the precise hand poses, geometry order, timing, reactions, framing or soundtrack.
Do not claim any source prompt, creator identity or generating model; those facts were not supplied.

instantiations.description: A clearly adult field researcher in a humid greenhouse draws an amber hand window that converts only enclosed leaves and clothing into cyan scientific cross-section linework, then dismisses it and watches one real flower open.

A clearly adult pastry chef frames a copper-lit workbench; only the enclosed dough, tools and apron become layered recipe-blueprint paper while the outside stays photographic, then the frame collapses and one real glaze highlight remains.

failure_modes.failure: The alternate medium spreads beyond the aperture.
failure_modes.repair: State hard clipping at the hand-defined edge and restate that every exterior pixel remains in the baseline medium.

failure_modes.failure: The effect floats away from the fingers.
failure_modes.repair: Bind each corner or active edge to a visible fingertip and make geometry changes follow the hand trajectory.

failure_modes.failure: Inside and outside no longer register to the same subject or space.
failure_modes.repair: Lock camera, pose, silhouette and background lines; change rendering only, not geometry or identity.

failure_modes.failure: Repeated shapes feel like arbitrary filters.
failure_modes.repair: Give every geometry a distinct proof region and preserve the same boundary physics across all states.

failure_modes.failure: The apex arrives too early or never resolves.
failure_modes.repair: Delay the largest coverage until late, hold it briefly, then show a visible contraction before baseline confirmation.

transfer_tests.finding: The hand-controlled clipping and release mechanism remains legible after changing identity, setting, palette, medium, proof regions, sound and payoff.
A craft setting and paper-blueprint medium preserve the causal aperture rule without retaining the source person's fashion styling or anime surface.

review.method: canonical-source English editorial pass with terminology, identity, and stable-token validation
